prerequisites: High school mathematics basics: vectors, derivatives and integrations, trigonometry.
First semester analysis and algebra courses: basics of mathematical analysis, differential calculus and linear algebra.

learning_outcomes.text: Master mathematical calculation tools for solving physics problems.
Analysis of a problem by mobilizing disciplinary concepts (Mobilize fundamental concepts to model, analyze and solve simple physics problems).

Implementation of disciplinary methods and tools (Interpret experimental data to consider their modeling, Validate a model by comparing its predictions with experimental results and Appreciate its validity limits, Identify sources of error to calculate uncertainty on an experimental result).
Be able to formalize a physics problem into an equation and apply appropriate mathematical tools to solve it.
Know the basics of point mechanics.
Learn to model a physical problem.
Identification of a problem within a disciplinary field (Propose analogies, make order of magnitude estimations and grasp their meaning, Manipulate the main mathematical tools useful in physics).
Be able to understand and solve point mechanics problems.

syllabus_topics: Kinematics with change of reference frames
Dynamics in Galilean and non-Galilean reference frames

assessment_methods.method: Continuous Assessment (for Applied Maths to Physics element)
